items.readable_text:
Content:
A composite polygon is a polygon that is made up of other polygons, such as triangles, parallelograms, rectangles, squares, and others.

Content:
For example, the polygon below is composite. How can we find its area?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e9ee72fb423022655fed82b4d3bfe887]

Content:
First, notice that the polygon consists of four squares and one rectangle in the middle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4295c67a47a9d643e16621d0f7b0e8ee]

Content:
To calculate the area of the composite polygon above, we add the areas of the four squares and the rectangle:

Content:
[MATH: A = 2A_{1} + 2A_{2} + A_{3}.]

Content:
The areas of the squares and the rectangle are
[MATH: A_{1}|= 3^{2} = 9,; A_{2}|= 2^{2} = 4,; A_{3}|= 3 ⋅ 2 = 6.]

Content:
So, the area of the entire figure is
[MATH: A|= 2 ⋅ 9 + 2 ⋅ 4 + 6; = 18 + 8 + 6; = 32.]

(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The figure is composed of three squares, [MATH: R_1,] [MATH: R_2,] and [MATH: R_3], and one rectangle, [MATH: R_4.]

The perimeter of the figure is determined by the sum of the lengths of

  • [MATH: 3] sides of [MATH: R_1] (each of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}]),

  • [MATH: 1] side of [MATH: R_2] (of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}]),

  • [MATH: 3] sides of [MATH: R_3] (of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}]),

  • [MATH: 3] sides of [MATH: R_4] (two of length [MATH: 3\,\textrm{cm}] and one of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}]).

Therefore, the perimeter is given by

[MATH: p|= 3 ⋅ 1 + 1 + 3 ⋅ 1 + (3 + 1 + 3); = 3 + 1 + 3 + 7; = 14cm.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

Therefore, the area of ​​the entire figure is [MATH: A|= A_{1} + A_{2}; = 3 + 6; = 9cm^{2}.]

items.title: Finding the Perimeter of a Composite Shape Given Its Area

sections.normalized_html:
The figure above is obtained by taking a square with an area of [MATH: 16\,\textrm{cm}^2] and cutting out an equilateral triangle. Find the perimeter of ​​the figure.

(Note: Figure not draw to scale)
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/2c9b28799f3f62222831c0b0253de6df]

The figure above is obtained by taking a square with an area of [MATH: 16\,\textrm{cm}^2] and cutting out an equilateral triangle. Find the perimeter of ​​the figure.

(Note: Figure not draw to scale)

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: a] be the length of the sides of the square. Then, the length of each side of the triangle is also [MATH: a] since it is equilateral and the square and the triangle have a common side.

We're given that the area of a square is [MATH: 16\,\textrm{cm}^2.] Therefore,

[MATH: a^{2}|= 16; a|= 4cm.]

The perimeter of the figure is the sum of the lengths of

  • [MATH: 3] sides of the square (each of length [MATH: a]), and

  • [MATH: 2] sides of the triangle (each of length [MATH: a]).

So, we have

[MATH: p = 3a + 2a = 5a.]

Finally, substituting [MATH: a=4\,\textrm{cm}] into the above, we get that the perimeter of ​​the given shape is [MATH: p|= 5a; = 5 ⋅ 4; = 20cm.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
A composite polygon is a polygon that is made up of other polygons, such as triangles, parallelograms, rectangles, squares, and others.

Content:
For example, the polygon below is composite. How can we find its area?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e9ee72fb423022655fed82b4d3bfe887]

Content:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4295c67a47a9d643e16621d0f7b0e8ee]

Content:
To calculate the area of the composite polygon above, we add the areas of the four squares and the rectangle:

Content:
[MATH: A = 2A_{1} + 2A_{2} + A_{3}.]

Content:
The areas of the squares and the rectangle are
[MATH: A_{1}|= 3^{2} = 9,; A_{2}|= 2^{2} = 4,; A_{3}|= 3 ⋅ 2 = 6.]

Content:
So, the area of the entire figure is
[MATH: A|= 2 ⋅ 9 + 2 ⋅ 4 + 6; = 18 + 8 + 6; = 32.]

---

The figure above is obtained by taking a square with an area of [MATH: 16\,\textrm{cm}^2] and cutting out an equilateral triangle. Find the perimeter of ​​the figure.

(Note: Figure not draw to scale)

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Let [MATH: a] be the length of the sides of the square. Then, the length of each side of the triangle is also [MATH: a] since it is equilateral and the square and the triangle have a common side.

[IMG: /graphics/07602bf09bdda323b4ad7c3f8c708ecd]

We're given that the area of a square is [MATH: 16\,\textrm{cm}^2.] Therefore,

[MATH: a^{2}|= 16; a|= 4cm.]

The perimeter of the figure is the sum of the lengths of

- [MATH: 3] sides of the square (each of length [MATH: a]), and
- [MATH: 2] sides of the triangle (each of length [MATH: a]).

So, we have

[MATH: p = 3a + 2a = 5a.]

Finally, substituting [MATH: a=4\,\textrm{cm}] into the above, we get that the perimeter of ​​the given shape is
[MATH: p|= 5a; = 5 ⋅ 4; = 20cm.]
